documents.title: Institutional AI Policy
documents.summary: UNE's overarching AI framework: shared definitions, nine guiding principles applying to faculty, staff and students, and governance by an AI Governance Committee. It sets no rule for AI in coursework and points to the AI Acceptable Use Policy and the faculty and student guidance for operational detail.
documents.stance_why: The policy sets principles and definitions and says 'More detailed operational expectations are set out in' other documents; it states no allowed or banned use for coursework, so it delegates.

units.why: States the policy's scope and purpose: 'overarching framework for AI use at UNE', so an institution-wide framework (P56) and informs.
units.anchor: This Institutional AI Policy provides the overarching framework for AI use at UNE.

units.why: A definition of AI ('Any machine-based system that autonomously performs tasks...') that sets what the policy covers, so P61 informs.
units.anchor: Any machine-based system that autonomously performs tasks commonly associated with human intelligence

units.why: Defines generative AI as covering embedded offerings, setting policy scope; P61 not P07 because it is a definition and does not tell anyone to disable or avoid embedded AI.
units.anchor: Generative AI includes both standalone offerings and offerings that are embedded in other software.

units.why: Defines agentic AI ('Autonomous systems designed to pursue complex goals') as a term used across the policy set, so P61.
units.anchor: Autonomous systems designed to pursue complex goals with minimal human intervention.

units.why: Defines 'enterprise private AI tools' as 'institutionally licensed AI tools', a definition (P61) that sets up later tool rules; it commands nothing itself.
units.anchor: institutionally licensed AI tools that community members access with their UNE credentials, not free tools

units.why: Defines 'High-risk data' (PHI, FERPA records, PII) as a scope term for the privacy rules, so P61 informs.
units.anchor: Data that requires the highest level of protection

units.why: Under Do No Harm, members are 'expected' to be 'promptly reporting any concerns about misuse, safety, or potential harm': a duty to report AI problems (P71).
units.anchor: promptly reporting any concerns about misuse, safety, or potential harm

units.why: Members are expected to choose data-protecting tools and be 'cautious about what information is entered', which is protecting data and preferring vetted tools (P50).
units.anchor: choosing tools that protect personal and institutional data, being cautious about what information is entered

units.why: 'Users are responsible for ... the actions and outcomes' says people own what AI helps produce (P29).
units.anchor: Users are responsible for ethical AI use and for the actions and outcomes that result

units.why: The Integrity principle lists 'being honest about when and how AI has been used', a general disclosure expectation (P24), phrased as expected conduct so 'should'.
units.anchor: being honest about when and how AI has been used

units.why: Members are expected to be 'correcting errors introduced by AI', which means checking and fixing AI output (P31).
units.anchor: correcting errors introduced by AI

units.why: 'seeking guidance when unsure about appropriate use' tells users to ask when unsure (P10).
units.anchor: seeking guidance when unsure about appropriate use

units.why: Transparency principle: 'avoiding secret or hidden use of AI where it affects others' is a rule to be open about AI use (P24).
units.anchor: avoiding secret or hidden use of AI where it affects others
units.policy: Members avoid secret or hidden use of AI where it affects others.

units.why: Collaboration principle encourages sharing practices and concerns internally across departments; it is not an outside coalition (P88) nor faculty support (P63), so no type fits.
units.anchor: encouraged to share effective practices, lessons learned, and concerns about AI use across departments and
units.uncovered_note: Community members are encouraged to share AI practices, lessons and concerns across departments and roles.

units.why: Autonomy principle: 'provide and seek clear information about when AI is being used' matches the right to know when AI is involved (P103).
units.anchor: All community members should provide and seek clear information about when AI is being used

units.why: Under Respect for Autonomy members should offer 'meaningful options to participate or opt out' of AI; opt-out rights are not covered by P51 (cost and access).
units.anchor: offering, where feasible, meaningful options to participate or opt out
units.uncovered_note: Where feasible, people are offered options to participate in or opt out of AI use and their preferences are honored.

units.why: 'expected to protect personal and confidential information when using AI tools' is a data-protection rule (P50).
units.anchor: protect personal and confidential information when using AI tools

units.why: 'using approved tools for sensitive data' tells everyone to use university-approved tools, institution-wide (P92).
units.anchor: using approved tools for sensitive data

units.why: Privacy principle includes 'following institutional policies and legal requirements', i.e. compliance with law and existing policy (P77).
units.anchor: following institutional policies and legal requirements

units.why: 'reporting any suspected privacy or security issues promptly' is a duty to report data exposure (P71).
units.anchor: reporting any suspected privacy or security issues promptly

units.why: Principle 7 asks members to weigh risks and benefits and stop uses with unacceptable risk. It is neither a monitoring system (P98) nor an approval process (P65), so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: assessing when human review is necessary, identifying where risks may outweigh benefits
units.uncovered_note: Members weigh benefits and risks before and while using AI, decide when human review is needed, and stop uses whose risks outweigh benefits.

units.why: 'commits to ongoing learning, reflection, and refinement' says practices will be revised (P54).
units.anchor: UNE commits to ongoing learning, reflection, and refinement of AI practices

units.why: 'encouraged to engage in training' is an encouragement to take AI training (P70).
units.anchor: All community members are encouraged to engage in training

units.why: Invites feedback to improve policies, so P54 (feedback invited).
units.anchor: provide feedback that can improve policies, tools, and practices over time

units.why: 'expected to avoid using AI in ways that deceive, manipulate, harass, or harm others' is a general conduct ban (P74).
units.anchor: avoid using AI in ways that deceive, manipulate, harass, or harm others

units.why: 'declining uses of AI that reinforce harmful biases' names bias harms as a reason to decline uses (P53).
units.anchor: declining uses of AI that reinforce harmful biases, erode trust

units.why: The same sentence tells members to avoid uses that 'shift responsibility away from human decision-makers' or 'obscure who is accountable'; this is about human accountability (P29) rather than consequential decisions about people (P73).
units.anchor: shift responsibility away from human decision-makers

units.why: Members decline uses that 'bypass meaningful learning', meaning AI should not replace the person's own learning (P32).
units.anchor: bypass meaningful learning and professional responsibilities

units.why: The Policy Statement names benefits ('significant opportunities to improve learning, increase efficiency') without a rule, so P87.
units.anchor: AI technologies offer significant opportunities to improve learning, increase efficiency, support innovation

units.why: The Introduction says UNE wants AI 'to improve efficiency and enable personalized learning', a benefit statement (P87).
units.anchor: enable personalized learning

units.why: States the human-centered principle that frames all UNE AI use, an institution-level principle (P56).
units.anchor: ensuring that UNE's educational environment remains fundamentally human-centered

units.why: Scope statement: the policies 'apply to all community members and use cases', so P56.
units.anchor: UNE has established clear guidelines and policies that apply to all community members and use

units.why: Everyone is 'expected to follow these standards, ensuring both legal compliance', a compliance expectation (P77).
units.anchor: Faculty, professional staff, and students are expected to follow these standards, ensuring both legal compliance

units.why: Names the AI Governance Committee as the body giving 'institutional oversight' of AI governance, i.e. who owns the policy (P80).
units.anchor: AI Governance Committee, in collaboration with academic and administrative leaders, provides institutional oversight

units.why: The Committee oversees 'enterprise AI tool approvals', which is review and approval of AI tools (P65). P80 is used for the ownership statement.
units.anchor: oversight for AI-related governance, standards, and enterprise AI tool approvals

units.why: Says the Committee administers the policy, naming who runs it (P80).
units.anchor: The AI Governance Committee Charter describes how the Committee administers this policy.

units.why: UNE says it is 'regularly reviewing and updating its policies', which is a revisit commitment (P54).
units.anchor: regularly reviewing and updating its policies to reflect technological advances, regulatory changes

units.why: Points to another document for the actual permitted and prohibited uses and sets no use rule itself, which reflects the framework role (P56).
units.anchor: Operational requirements, permitted uses, prohibited uses, data protection requirements, and compliance expectations are set forth
units.fit_note: The unit delegates operational rules to another document that was not collected.

units.why: A fixed annual review cycle, so P54.
units.anchor: This policy will be reviewed at least annually and updated as needed

documents.title: AI Policy Guidance for Faculty
documents.summary: Guidance telling UNE faculty to put an AI policy in every syllabus, explain its rationale, teach citation, disclose their own AI use, and avoid relying on AI detectors. An appendix gives three syllabus templates (restricted, integrated with restrictions, open) sharing a six-part structure.

units.why: 'consider how using or restricting AI will help students meet learning outcomes' ties the rule to learning objectives (P83).
units.anchor: Faculty should consider how using or restricting AI will help students meet learning outcomes.

units.why: 'required all faculty members to articulate a policy on AI use in each of their syllabi' is the syllabus-statement requirement (P09).
units.anchor: UNE has required all faculty members to articulate a policy on AI use in each

units.anchor: encouraged to provide explicit examples of acceptable and prohibited uses of AI tools
units.fit_note: Encouragement to give examples, not a duty to include a statement.

units.why: Faculty 'are encouraged to integrate AI into their teaching', which welcomes AI by default for teaching (P02).
units.anchor: encouraged to integrate AI into their teaching in intentional ways that foster critical thinking
units.fit_note: Addressed to faculty teaching, not to students' use.

units.why: 'to enhance, not replace, their learning' says AI should not replace the student's thinking (P32).
units.anchor: learning to use AI responsibly to enhance, not replace, their learning

units.anchor: UNE will support this work through robust professional development

units.why: 'open discussions with students about the rationale' is explaining and discussing the rules (P66).

units.why: Says making policy requires faculty to 'engage with students'. It is not co-creation, so P66 not P67.

documents.title: AI Policy Guidance for Students
documents.summary: Student-facing guidance explaining that each course sets its own AI rule, along with four expectations shared by every course: disclosure, responsibility, privacy and IP, and consequences for misuse. It also covers approved tools, data protection, research use, detection tools, accessibility and where to get help.
documents.stance_why: The text says 'Your instructor determines how AI may be used' and lists three course approaches, so it delegates the stance to instructors and names tiers.

units.anchor: students are encouraged to develop the knowledge and judgment needed to use it thoughtfully
units.fit_note: Encourages developing judgment to use AI, not unconditional use.

units.why: Treats AI literacy as a curricular goal for students (P70).
units.anchor: AI literacy is a hallmark of a UNE education.

units.why: 'you remain responsible for what you submit' is ownership (P29).
units.anchor: you remain responsible for what you submit, the decisions you make, and how you use
